description: Understanding junctional rhythms and their clinical significance
overview: This module covers junctional rhythms including junctional escape rhythm, accelerated junctional rhythm, and junctional tachycardia.
objectives: Learn clinical implications of junctional rhythms

slides.title: Junctional Escape Rhythm
slides.content: Junctional escape rhythm: rate 40-60 bpm, narrow QRS, inverted or absent P waves, regular rhythm. Occurs when higher pacemakers fail.

slides.title: Accelerated Junctional Rhythm
slides.content: Accelerated junctional rhythm: rate 60-100 bpm, narrow QRS, inverted P waves, regular rhythm. May be caused by digitalis toxicity.

quiz.question: What is the rate range for accelerated junctional rhythm?
quiz.explanation: Accelerated junctional rhythm has a rate of 60-100 bpm.

slides.title: Junctional Tachycardia
slides.content: Junctional tachycardia: rate >100 bpm, narrow QRS, inverted P waves, regular rhythm. May be paroxysmal or sustained.

quiz.question: What characterizes junctional tachycardia?
quiz.explanation: Junctional tachycardia is characterized by a rate greater than 100 bpm.

slides.title: Clinical Significance
slides.content: Clinical significance: junctional rhythms may indicate underlying heart disease, medication effects, or electrolyte abnormalities. Treatment depends on cause and symptoms.

quiz.question: What can cause accelerated junctional rhythm?
quiz.explanation: Accelerated junctional rhythm can be caused by various factors including digitalis toxicity and electrolyte abnormalities.
